In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the atmospheric Pb deposition in Switzerland increased by 2 orders of magnitude from pre-industrial times to the 1980s.

the atmospheric Pb deposition in the five Swiss peat cores is characterized by two major enrichment periods:  one during the late nineteenth century and one between the late 1950s and the early 1970s.
the Pb enrichment factors and fluxes in western Switzerland were generally higher than in central Switzerland.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pb deposition in Switzerland has increased 100-fold over the last 200 years and that Pb isotope ratios have been used to trace Pb sources.

the atmospheric Pb deposition since the industrial revolution in western and central Swiss rural areas has been characterized by two distinct periods of enrichment relative to the background: between 1880–1920 with enrichment factors ranging from 40–80, and between 1950 and 1985 with enrichment factors ranging 80–100.
the atmospheric Pb deposition has increased since the Industrial Revolution, and that the fluxes and the isotopic composition of the peat cores reflect this increase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Pb deposition has declined in Switzerland since the 1980s.

peat cores can be used to study the history of atmospheric Pb deposition, but that the results are highly dependent on the location of the site, on the type of peat, on the sampling strategy and on the analytical technique.

the isotopic composition of Pb is a very powerful tool in reconstructing past emissions of Pb from human activities, and that the isotopic compositions in peat cores can be used to identify the main sources of Pb in the past, and to distinguish between the effects of the Industrial Revolution and the introduction of Pb in gasoline.
